source_claim.statement: For symmetric bounded paired coefficients, carry asymmetry can occur only at coefficient 9; in particular, absence of 9 implies the exact integer J is zero. The converse need not hold.

target_statement: For q : Nat -> Nat and L : Nat define outgoing q L = (List.range L).map (fun i => DecimalDigits.carry q (i+1)); actualCharge q L is the existing exact parity-selected U/S carryCharge of that list.
Under hb : forall i < L, q i <= 18, prove outgoing has exactly L entries, gives the existing computed outgoing carries, is binary, and actualCharge=0 iff forall i<L, carry q (i+1)=carry q (L-i).
Under hb and hs : forall i<L, q i = q (L-1-i), reuse RawSymmetryObstruction.nonnine_binary_div to prove q i != 9 implies equality of those reflected outgoing carries.
Under hb and hs, derive actualCharge != 0 iff exists i<L, q i=9 and carry q(i+1) != carry q(L-i); consequently no coefficient 9 implies actualCharge=0.
